explain.say: Blushing is when your face, ears and neck go red and warm, usually when you feel embarrassed or noticed. It happens on its own: you can't switch it on or off by trying.

faq.q: Why does blood rush to your face when you blush?
faq.a: During a blush, signals from the fight-or-flight nerves make the small blood vessels in the face widen, so more blood flows through them. The cheeks have many vessels near the surface, so they look red.
asks: Tell me about face vessels widening

faq.a: Feeling embarrassed, self-conscious, praised or the centre of attention triggers the sympathetic, or fight-or-flight, nervous system, which causes the blood vessels in the face to widen.
asks: Tell me about the alarm nerves firing

faq.a: Not directly. Blushing is controlled automatically by the nervous system, and worrying about blushing can even make it more likely.
As far as scientists know, only humans blush from embarrassment. Some ideas suggest it evolved as a visible signal that we know we've made a social mistake.

faq.q: Why do you feel hot when you blush?
faq.a: The extra blood flowing near the skin of your face brings body heat with it, so your cheeks feel warm.
asks: Why do my cheeks feel warm when embarrassed?

facts: Charles Darwin wrote in 1872 that blushing is the most peculiar and most human of all expressions.
Blushing is controlled by the sympathetic nervous system.

quiz.say: What happens to the blood vessels in your cheeks when you blush?

options.show: They widen and fill with more blood
options.say: They widen and fill with more blood

quiz.why: Wider vessels let more warm blood flow near the surface, which shows as red.

wrong.0: Narrower vessels would make the skin paler, not redder.
wrong.2: Blood keeps flowing; there is actually more of it.
